title: Feature patchbook — microbehaviors & lightweight rollouts
content:
Purpose / quick pitch:
This is a lightweight, reusable collection (a "patchbook") of small, opinionated runtime + API feature toggles and UX affordances we can ship quickly to tune cost/latency/quality tradeoffs for different customer archetypes. Think: 8–12 small knobs we can mix and match for canaries and A/Bs instead of launching full product lanes.

Why do this?
- We keep shipping incremental improvements that matter to customers (lower cost, faster responses) without large PRDs.
- Enables faster experiments that combine server/runtime changes + API UX (e.g., compact-mode + client hint header).
- Platform teams can adopt patterns rather than re-implement feature-by-feature.

Target outcomes (hypotheses):
1) Average per-request token cost for selected workloads reduces by 10–25% with <5% measured user-perceived quality regression.
2) Time-to-A/B-launch for small inference experiments drops to <2 weeks (from idea to traffic split).
3) Customers on lower tiers adopt at least one patchbook mode within 3 months when offered as a simple opt-in.

Audience / users:
- Product teams shipping chat assistants with incremental QoS/price tradeoffs.
- Platform customers (internal and external) who want quick toggles for cost/reliability during events.
- Solutions engineering: quick toolkit for customizing behavior per-customer.

Patchbook primitives (initial list) — short descriptions + early ideas for experiments:
1) Compact-response-mode (server + client-hint header)
   - What: favor short, concise responses; enforce token budget at runtime + response truncation heuristics.
   - UX: client sets X-Response-Mode: compact or prompt param compact=true
   - Quick metric: median response tokens, NPS for conciseness (survey), task success on closed benchmarks

2) Progressive-fidelity (fast preview + optional full)
   - What: return a first-pass short answer (low-cost model) and push longer answer async or via follow-up request
   - Hooks: streaming-first-frame + follow-up endpoint id

3) Token-anchoring (prefix caching + deterministic trimming)
   - What: automated prefix cache lookup + allowed eviction policies tailored to session type
   - Runtime note: KV cache TTLs + eviction heuristics per-customer tier

4) Economical-decoder (sampling + temperature ceilings for cost spikes)
   - What: dynamic sampling settings based on estimated output length and cost budget
   - UX: hint param to prefer deterministic vs. economical

5) Micro-rollout guard (traffic shard + fallback path)
   - What: rollout by user segment with automatic fallback to baseline model when SLOs breached
   - Metrics: fallback rate, latency delta, error rate by shard

6) Compact-structuring (structured responses instead of free text when possible)
   - What: prefer JSON/fields output for data tasks to reduce tokens and postprocessing cost

7) Early-stopping heuristics (semantically-aware stop)
   - What: stop generation when semantic confidence threshold met (score from a small classifier)

8) Response-pruning (post-gen trimming preserving key facts)
   - What: algorithmic compress-then-trim to drop non-essential sentences while preserving entities/intents

User stories (examples):
- As a PM of a consumer chat product, I want a low-cost reply mode so I can offer a cheaper plan tier without overhauling prompts.
- As an SRE, I want to canary compact-response-mode on 5% of traffic and automatically cork traffic if p95 latency increases >100ms.
- As a Solutions Engineer, I want to offer a customer a preview rollout that returns first-pass answers quickly and charges only if they request the full answer.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP patchbook v0):
- We have server-side flags/hints to toggle at least 3 primitives (compact-response, progressive-fidelity, micro-rollout)
- Real traffic A/B harness exists: can route 1–10% traffic and record fallback/quality signals to dashboards
- Basic SDK support: example snippet for JS python for client hint header and post-followup fetch
- Experiment dashboard: per-variant token cost, latency p50/p95, fallback rate, simple quality signal (keyword-match / small eval)

Quality signal options (cheap):
- Keyword preservation rate on a small set of prompts (synthetic)
- Automatic BLEU-like or semantic-similarity score (embed cosine) against golden answers (sampled)
- Small human eval panel for top-2 risky experiments

Quick rollout plan / timeline (very rough):
- Week 0: pick 3 primitives + quick spec (this doc) + identify 2 pilot teams
- Week 1–2: runtime + API flags implemented; SDK example; small internal canary (internal product)
- Week 3–4: public A/B for 5–10% traffic for one customer archetype; collect metrics
- Week 5: iterate or rollback based on thresholds; document playbook for other teams

Technical notes / runbook fragments:
- API: accept header X-Redwood-Patchbook: compact=v1; progressive=preview-token-budget:200
- Routing: feature flags on route-level in Console; create a templated rollout that pairs variant -> fallback model
- Tracing: attach experiment id to spans, capture token counts as metrics (prometheus label: experiment_id)
- Data retention: mark all outputs from experiments for short retention (30d) and opt-out for PII-heavy customers

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve before dev):
- Who bears cost for progressive-fidelity second fetch? Should we charge on full answer only? (billing ops)
- How much of the logic lives in runtime vs model prompt engineering? (SRE + Applied ML)
- What is acceptable quality delta per archetype? (product + sales input)
- Guardrails for structured outputs (we need schema validation to avoid malformed JSON responses)

Experiment ideas (quick hacks):
- Toggle: compact + embed-shortening: run embed on trimmed output and compare similarity to baseline
- Event-based auto-fallthrough: if fallback rate >2% in 5m window, route new requests to baseline for 15min
- Customer-facing opt-in modal offering "Budget Mode" that shows estimated cost savings (very rough)

Early metrics to track (baseline + experiment):
- token_count_per_session (median, p90)
- cost_per_1k_requests
- latency_p50/p95
- fallback_rate
- simple_quality_score (embed cosine vs golden)

Next steps / todo (for me):
- [ ] split this into a short deck for PM sync (1 slide per primitive + hypothesis) (due: 2025-12-05)
- [ ] open GitHub RFC describing server flags and minimal SDK API (assign to @noah)
- [ ] book quick sync with Applied ML to discuss progressive-fidelity risk matrix
- [ ] draft Console rollout template and default thresholds (p95 latency + fallback rate)

Notes to self / rough ideas to capture:
- Could productize these as "patchbook recipes" in Console so customers click pre-built mixes (e.g., "Frugal chat", "Fast preview")
- Keep primitives orthogonal: allow mixing compact+progressive; avoid couples that conflict (don't pair structural-only with compact truncation by default)
- Consider a simple "cost-estimate API" that returns expected token delta before enabling a patchbook recipe

Random scribbles:
- Try proof-of-concept by using a small Llama2-like fast model for previews + running an embed-based similarity check to gate full answer
- Need a BFF endpoint that can orchestrate preview->full flow without user needing to wire two calls

End of scratch.

(If this feels useful I'll split into a short RFC + quick canary checklist next.)
